sentences.text: Net revenue, measured as net interest income plus noninterest income, grew from $96.6 billion in FY2016 [D5] to $182 billion in FY2025 [D206], with net interest income compounding at 8.4% [F111] and noninterest income at 6.2% [F112].
Net income compounded at 9.7% [F113] and diluted EPS at 13.9% [F115], as the diluted share count fell from 3,649.8 million [X83] to 2,781.5 million [X92].

The window is cyclical rather than a steady climb: net interest income fell 4.7% in FY2020 [D100] while the provision reached 14.6% of revenue [D88], and net income then rose 65.8% in FY2021 [D118] alongside a $9.3 billion provision release [X143].

Net interest income then rose 27.5% in FY2022 [D149] and 33.8% in FY2023 [D174]; segment filings attribute this to deposit margin expansion on higher rates [P50][P37], and the pack holds no firmwide passage for either move.
Bank revenue rose 2.8% in FY2025 [D226], with net interest income up 3.1% [D221] and noninterest income up 2.4% [D222].

Net interest income of $95.4 billion [F10] reflects higher Markets net interest income, Card revolving balances and wholesale deposits, largely offset by deposit margin compression and lower rates [P28]; excluding Markets it was $92.6 billion, flat year on year [P28].

Noninterest income of $87.0 billion [F20] rose 2.4% [D222] even though the filing names the absence of the $7.9 billion Visa gain recorded in 2024 as the main offset to higher Markets and asset-management fees [P27].
North America supplied 76.6% of FY2025 revenue [D249], while Asia-Pacific was the fastest-growing region at 17.3% [D300], adding 1.2pp to revenue growth [D301].
Diluted EPS rose 1.4% [D216] while net income fell 2.6% [D214], as the diluted share count dropped 3.4% [D224]; the table's net income is proxy-sourced [R1].
The FY2025 efficiency ratio was 52.4% [D207], 0.7pp above the window low of 51.7% [D331] and 4.8pp below the window median of 57.2% [D333].
The banks peer median is 61.7% [D337], so the ratio sits 9.3pp below it [D207].

Noninterest expense rose 4.2% to $95.6 billion [D225][X137] against revenue growth of 2.8% [D226], on higher compensation, brokerage and technology spending [P26], partly offset by $763 million of FDIC accrual releases [P26].

The provision rose from $10.7 billion [X146] to $14.2 billion [X147], or 7.8% of revenue [D208] against a peer median of 6.0% [D341]; segment filings tie the increase to Card Services charge-offs and loan growth [P18].
Operating cash flow was -$147.8 billion in FY2025 [F60] against net income of $57.0 billion [F30]; for a bank this is not a meaningful measure of earnings quality.
The outflow reflects higher trading assets and securities borrowed, partly offset by net income [P21][P23][F60].
Capital return of $48.2 billion [D205], made up of $31.6 billion of buybacks [X102] and $16.6 billion of dividends [X112], equalled 84.6% of net income [D205][F30].
The pack has no capital expenditure line, so capital intensity cannot be measured; depreciation and amortization was $8.8 billion [X40].

Shareholders' equity reached $362 billion in FY2025 [F110], up 5.1% [D220], and return on average equity of 16.1% [D213] sat at the 100th percentile of the banks peer group against a median of 11.8% [D338][D339].
Loans of $1.47 trillion [X197] equalled 57.3% of deposits [D211], up from 43.1% in FY2021 [D115], and the 10-K cites about $449 billion of available FHLB and discount-window capacity [P9].
Diluted shares fell 3.4% to 2,781.5 million [D224][X92] while buybacks rose to $31.6 billion from $18.8 billion [X102][X101].
The FY2023 acquisitions cost $9.9 billion [X115], and the filing ties First Republic costs to noninterest expense of $87.2 billion [P42][X135].
Provision for credit losses has risen each year since FY2022, from 5.0% of revenue [D136] to 7.8% in FY2025 [D208].
Nonperforming exposure rose $478 million on downgrades in Technology, Media & Telecommunications, Oil & Gas and Utilities [P3].
Credit cost, rather than operating margin, is the variable most likely to erode the revenue gains behind the FY2025 result [D208].
Operating cash flow has been negative for two years running, at -$42.0 billion in FY2024 [F59] and -$147.8 billion in FY2025 [F60], driven by trading and securities balances [P21].

Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded, with 10-K differences of up to 0.10% [R1]; the conclusions here hold, but the 10-K figures should be cited where precision matters.
Net interest income growth slowed to 3.1% [D221] from 3.7% [D197], and deposit margin compression from lower rates and funds transfer pricing is cited as the driver [P20].

Provision as a share of revenue: a fall from 7.8% [D208] toward the peer median of 6.0% [D341] would show credit costs easing, while a further rise above 7.8% [D208] would confirm the trend; the FY2026 10-K will show it.

Efficiency ratio: holding below the FY2025 level of 52.4% [D207] keeps the cost discipline seen since FY2024 [D331]; a move back toward the window median of 57.2% [D333] would reverse it, and the FY2026 10-K will show it.

Net interest income excluding Markets: a reading flat against the FY2025 level of $92.6 billion [P28] would confirm slowing core spread income, while growth above that level would reverse the concern; the FY2026 10-K will show it.
